newsitem.title: UK: UK minister says relaxed about earnings growth.
newsitem.headline: UK minister says relaxed about earnings growth.

text.p: UK employment minister Eric Forth said the government was pretty relaxed about wage rises despite a rise in underlying average earnings to 4.0 percent in August.
Asked in an interview with Reuters Financial Television if the figures meant Britain now had wage inflation, he replied:

"I don't think so. I have talked at length to my experts about this and they are pretty relaxed. They point out that the average earnings figure has been between three and four percent for about three years now."
"We at this stage don't see any signs of overheating," Forth added. "It's probably on the high side from what one would ideally want but we don't think that there is a danger sign here."
He did not believe the rise in average earnings represented a threat to the underlying rate of inflation. A four percent increase in average earnings was "manageable and containable."
The good news was that the traditional expectation that falling unemployment would put irresistible pressure on earnings did not seem to apply, Forth said.
Asked if he was suggesting that average earnings could moderate in future, Forth replied: "I don't see any reason why not."
But he added that it was futile to try to project earnings figures.
